image_description: A group of Australian Pelicans standing on a sandy shore next to a body of blue water. The birds display characteristic white plumage with black flight feathers and pinkish bills. One pelican in the center stands tall, while others are positioned around it, some facing away or partially cropped by the frame edges.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bill with distensible gular pouch extending from lower mandible.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The central pelican clearly displays the signature long bill and the visible outline of the gular pouch beneath the lower mandible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bill is enormous and elongated, vastly exceeding head length, with bright orange, yellow, or pink coloration during breeding.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bills are distinctly longer than the heads and exhibit the pale pink/flesh tone typical of Australian Pelicans.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is large with prominent pouch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Proportions of the head relative to the body and the visible pouch structure match the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Plumage is predominantly white, grey, or brown depending on species and season.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The birds are primarily white with black markings on the wings, consistent with adult Australian Pelican plumage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body exhibits heavy barrel-shaped torso of very large proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The central bird shows the characteristic bulky, boat-like body shape of a pelican.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wings are extremely broad and long with dark flight feathers contrasting lighter body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Dark primary/secondary feathers are clearly visible against the white body on the folded wings of the foreground and central birds.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and webbed with all four toes connected.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While legs are visible on the leftmost bird, the resolution is insufficient to verify the specific 'four toes connected' (totipalmate) anatomy. The feature is testable but not clearly present/verifiable at this scale.
The central pelican exhibits the classic retracted S-curve neck posture.
The tail feathers are short and appear wedge-shaped on the bird in the lower right foreground.

The connection between the legs and the sand is slightly muddy; the toes blend into the ground texture rather than having distinct separation.
